chunks: 2673 - And it was narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn al-Mughīrah, who said:

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan al-Awwal عليه السلام: “May I use shade while I am in ihram?” He said: “No.” I said: “Then may I use shade and offer expiation?” He said: “No.” I said: “Then if I become ill?” He said: “Use shade and offer expiation.”

Then he said: “Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم said: ‘There is no pilgrim who remains exposed to the sun while reciting the talbiyah until the sun sets except that his sins depart with it.’”

key_terms.أُظَلِّلُ: I seek or use shade over myself.
key_terms.أُكَفِّرُ: I offer expiation for violating a ruling.
key_terms.مُحْرِمٌ: A person in the state of ihram for hajj or ʿumrah.

ai.seo_question: Can a muhrim use shade during hajj, and what if he is ill?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling regarding using shade while in ihram during hajj. It prohibits shading oneself in the normal case, permits it with expiation in illness, and explains the spiritual merit of enduring the sun while in talbiyah through a saying of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2673 - It was narrated from Abdullah ibn al-Mughira, who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan the First (as): "Can I use a shade while I am in Ihram?"
Imam (as) said: "No."
I asked: "What if I use a shade and offer expiation?"
Imam (as) said: "No."
I asked: "What if I fall ill?"
Imam (as) said: "Use a shade and offer expiation."

Then Imam (as) said: "Do you not know that the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no pilgrim who exposes himself to the sun while reciting the Talbiyah until the sun sets except that his sins disappear with the setting of the sun.'"
